newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Republican lawmakers boycott Gore address.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Republican lawmakers boycott Gore address.

text.p: Scores of Republican lawmakers on Thursday boycotted an appearance by Vice President Al Gore, saying they would not be part of what they called a thinly disguised fund-raising junket.
Only 17 of the state's 55 Republican legislators attended an appearance by Gore at the California Legislature, where Gore called for bipartisan support for school reforms.
No formal boycott was called by Republicans, according to a spokesman for state Assembly Republican Leader Curt Pringle.

Rather, many Republican legislators chose not to attend the speech because they saw Gore's visit as an attempt to raise his political profile for a possible presidential bid in 2000, said John Nelson, a spokesman for Pringle.

After addressing the state legislature, Gore appeared at a $1,000-a-person luncheon hosted by the state Democratic Party. Gore has been the target of criticism over his admission that he made questionable telephone calls in 1995 from his White House office soliciting money for Democrats.

"It has become obvious to me that the vice president's brief appearance in the state Capitol today is intended solely to provide a veneer of propriety to a day crammed with partisan political fundraising," Republican Assemblyman Tom McClintock said. "I will not be a party to this debasement of the office of the vice presidency."
Democrats, who invited Gore to the legislature, criticised the Republicans for dodging the vice president's address.

"This shows a real pettiness on their part," said Sandy Harrison, a spokesman for Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat. "Gore came here to talk about education, but to some of our Republican legislators, they were more concerned with petty politics."
During the address, Gore urged California lawmakers to adopt the Clinton Administration's proposed education standards and called for a "citizens' army" of reading tutors.
